# EFF Sues for Answers About Medicare's AI Experiment

SAN FRANCISCO – The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) today filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit against the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) seeking records about a multi-state program that is using AI to evaluate requests for medical care.

"Tasking an algorithm with making determinations about treatment can create unwarranted—and even discriminatory—delays or denials of necessary medical care," said Kit Walsh, EFF’s Director of AI and Access-to-Knowledge Legal Projects. "Given these serious risks, the public requires transparency that it hasn't gotten. We're suing to get badly needed answers about how Medicare's AI experiment works."

Announced by CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz last year, the pilot program known as WISeR (Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction) uses AI to assess prior authorization requests from Medicare beneficiaries. Previously rare in original Medicare, prior authorization requires medical providers to obtain advance approval from a patient’s health insurer before delivering certain treatments or services as a condition of coverage.

Unfortunately, there is little information about how the AI algorithms used in WISeR work, including what training data they rely on. It remains unclear whether WISeR has any safeguards against systemic flaws such as algorithmic bias, privacy violations, and wrongful denials of care.

Healthcare experts, care providers, and lawmakers have all raised alarms that WISeR may cause serious harm to patients by relying on AI unless it has the necessary safeguards. Despite this widespread criticism, WISeR was rolled out in six states in January, potentially affecting as many as 6.4 million Medicare beneficiaries, according to  [one estimate](https://www.mcdermottplus.com/blog/regs-eggs/three-key-takeaways-from-the-cms-innovation-centers-new-wiser-model/) .

By design, WISeR incentivizes contracted companies to deny prior approval against the best interests of patients. Vendors are compensated, in part, on the volume of healthcare services they deny and are entitled to as much as 20 percent of the associated savings. Just weeks after WISeR's launch, hospitals and other health care providers  [started reporting](https://www.modernhealthcare.com/politics-regulation/mh-cms-wiser-medicare-prior-authorizations/)  delays in care approval, communication gaps, and administrative strain.

Earlier this year, EFF submitted a FOIA request to CMS asking for records related to WISeR. Among other records, the request sought agreements with software vendors participating in WISeR; records related to any tests for accuracy, bias, or hallucinations in vendors' technology; and records related to any audits, monitoring, or evaluation of WISeR and participating vendors. To date, CMS has not provided any of these records to EFF. EFF's FOIA lawsuit asks for their immediate processing and release.

"The public has a right to know more about the algorithms driving decisions around their healthcare," said Tori Noble, Staff Attorney at EFF. "Without greater transparency, patients, providers, and policymakers will continue to be left in the dark.”

*EFF thanks Stanford Law School's Juelsgaard Intellectual Property & Innovation Clinic for their help in preparing this lawsuit.***For the complaint:**[https://www.eff.org/document/complaint-eff-v-cms-medicare-wiser-foia](https://www.eff.org/document/complaint-eff-v-cms-medicare-wiser-foia)

# EFF 提告，要求公開 Medicare「AI 實驗」的答案

舊金山——電子前哨基金會（Electronic Frontier Foundation，EFF）今天依《資訊自由法》（Freedom of Information Act，FOIA）對美國醫療保險與醫療補助服務中心（Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services，CMS）提起訴訟，要求取得一項跨州計畫的相關紀錄；該計畫正使用 AI 評估醫療照護申請。

「把治療判定交給演算法，可能造成必要醫療照護被不當、甚至帶有歧視地延誤或拒絕，」EFF 的 AI 與知識取得法律專案主任 Kit Walsh 表示。「鑑於這些嚴重風險，公眾需要透明度，但至今並未得到。我們提告，是為了取得迫切需要的答案，了解 Medicare 的 AI 實驗到底如何運作。」

這項試辦計畫由 CMS 署長 Mehmet Oz 博士去年宣布，名為 WISeR（Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction，浪費與不適當服務減量），使用 AI 評估 Medicare 受益人的事前授權申請。事前授權過去在傳統 Medicare（original Medicare）中相當少見；它要求醫療服務提供者在提供特定治療或服務之前，先取得病患健康保險方的事先核准，作為保險給付的條件。

遺憾的是，外界對 WISeR 使用的 AI 演算法如何運作所知甚少，包括它們仰賴哪些訓練資料。目前也仍不清楚 WISeR 是否設有任何防範系統性缺陷的保護措施，例如演算法偏誤、隱私侵害，以及錯誤拒絕照護。

醫療照護專家、照護提供者與立法者都已提出警告：若 WISeR 在沒有必要保護措施的情況下仰賴 AI，可能會對病患造成嚴重傷害。儘管面臨廣泛批評，WISeR 仍於 1 月在六個州上路；根據[一項估算](https://www.mcdermottplus.com/blog/regs-eggs/three-key-takeaways-from-the-cms-innovation-centers-new-wiser-model/)，可能影響多達 640 萬名 Medicare 受益人。

WISeR 在設計上會鼓勵簽約公司違背病患的最佳利益，拒絕事前核准。廠商的報酬有一部分取決於他們拒絕的醫療服務量，並且有權取得相關節省金額最高 20% 的分成。WISeR 推出短短幾週後，醫院和其他醫療照護提供者就 [開始通報](https://www.modernhealthcare.com/politics-regulation/mh-cms-wiser-medicare-prior-authorizations/) 照護核准延遲、溝通落差，以及行政負擔增加等問題。

今年稍早，EFF 向 CMS 提交《資訊自由法》（FOIA）申請，要求取得與 WISeR 相關的紀錄。除其他紀錄外，該申請也要求提供參與 WISeR 的軟體廠商協議、與廠商技術中任何準確性、偏誤或幻覺測試相關的紀錄，以及與 WISeR 和參與廠商的任何稽核、監督或評估相關的紀錄。截至目前，CMS 尚未向 EFF 提供任何這些紀錄。EFF 的 FOIA 訴訟要求立即處理並公開這些紀錄。

「大眾有權進一步了解那些左右其醫療照護決策的演算法，」EFF 專職律師 Tori Noble 表示。「若沒有更高的透明度，病患、醫療照護提供者和政策制定者將持續被蒙在鼓裡。」

*EFF 感謝史丹佛法學院 Juelsgaard Intellectual Property & Innovation Clinic 協助準備本訴訟。***起訴狀：**[https://www.eff.org/document/complaint-eff-v-cms-medicare-wiser-foia](https://www.eff.org/document/complaint-eff-v-cms-medicare-wiser-foia)
